Laravel Boost guidelines for Laravel 12, Prompts 0, MCP 0, Pint 1, Sail 1, PHPUnit 11. Follow project conventions; inspect sibling files, use descriptive names, and reuse components. Stick to existing directories; don't create base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove it works. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise.

Use Laravel Boost tools. Before code changes, search Laravel-ecosystem documentation with `search-docs`; use it before other approaches. Pass package arrays when relevant. Start with multiple broad, simple topic queries; don't include package names. Search supports stemming, AND terms, quoted phrases, mixed queries, and multiple queries (any term). Use `list-artisan-commands` to check Artisan parameters. Use `get-absolute-url` for project URLs; `tinker` to execute PHP/debug or query Eloquent; `database-query` for read-only database access; `browser-logs` for browser errors. Only recent browser logs will be useful - ignore old logs. If frontend changes aren't visible, ask whether they need `bun run build`, `bun run dev`, or `composer run dev`.

PHP: Always use braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion; do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters. Use explicit return types and parameter types. Prefer PHPDoc over comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless there is something _very_ complex going on. Add array shapes when useful. Enum keys are typically TitleCase.

Laravel:
- Use `php artisan make:` to create files; use `php artisan make:class` for generic PHP classes. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and correct `--options`.
- Use typed Eloquent relationships; prefer relationships and models over raw queries, manual joins, or `DB::`. Use query builder for very complex operations and eager-load to prevent N+1s.
- For new models, create useful factories and seeders; ask whether more are needed and check `list-artisan-commands` for `php artisan make:model` options.
- APIs default to versioned Eloquent API Resources unless existing conventions differ. Use Form Requests (rules and custom messages) rather than inline controller validation; follow sibling rules format.
- Use `ShouldQueue` jobs for time-consuming work and built-in auth/authorization (gates, policies, Sanctum, etc.). Prefer named routes and `route()`.
- Use environment variables only in configuration files - never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files. Always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`.
- Tests should use factories and existing factory states. Follow existing Faker style (`$this->faker` or `fake()`).
- Create tests with `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; use `--unit` for unit tests. Most tests should be feature tests.
- For `Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest`, run `bun run build` or ask the user to run `bun run dev` or `composer run dev`.
- Use Laravel 11 streamlined structure: No middleware files in `app/Http/Middleware/`. Register middleware, exceptions, and routing in `bootstrap/app.php`; providers in `bootstrap/providers.php`. **No app\Console\Kernel.php** - use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php` for console configuration. **Commands auto-register** from `app/Console/Commands/`.
- Column-altering migrations must retain all previously defined column attributes. Eager-load limits are native: `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Prefer model `casts()` over `$casts` when consistent with sibling models.

Pint: You must run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty` before finalizing changes to ensure your code matches the project's expected style. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint` to fix any formatting issues.

PHPUnit: All tests must be written as PHPUnit classes. Use `php artisan make:test --phpunit {name}`. If you see a test using "Pest", convert it to PHPUnit. Every time a test has been updated, run that singular test. Test happy, failure, and weird paths. You must not remove any tests or test files from the tests directory without approval. Run the minimal number of tests, using an appropriate filter, before finalizing. Commands: `php artisan test`; `php artisan test tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php`; `php artisan test --filter=testName`. When feature tests pass, ask whether the user would like to run the full suite.

Tailwind: Follow project conventions, use Tailwind classes, and offer to extract repeated patterns into convention-matching components. Consider class order, priority, defaults, redundancy, and logical grouping. Use gap utilities for lists, not margins. Match existing dark mode support with `dark:`. Always use Tailwind CSS v4 - do not use deprecated utilities. `corePlugins` is not supported in Tailwind v4. Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first configuration with the `<REDACTED_USER>` directive; no separate `tailwind.config.js` is needed. Import with a regular CSS `<REDACTED_USER>` statement, not v3 directives. Theme example: `--color-brand: oklch(0.72 0.11 178);`; import example: `<REDACTED_USER> "tailwindcss";` (not `@tailwind base;`, `@tailwind components;`, `@tailwind utilities;`). Tailwind v4 removed deprecated utilities. Do not use the deprecated option - use the replacement: `bg-opacity-*` → `bg-black/*`; `text-opacity-*` → `text-black/*`; `border-opacity-*` → `border-black/*`; `divide-opacity-*` → `divide-black/*`; `ring-opacity-*` → `ring-black/*`; `placeholder-opacity-*` → `placeholder-black/*`; `flex-shrink-*` → `shrink-*`; `flex-grow-*` → `grow-*`; `overflow-ellipsis` → `text-ellipsis`;
